title: He was chosen…
paragraphs:
He was chosen…
and still tried to say no.
“I can’t speak.”
Let that hit.

Because the real battle wasn’t Pharaoh.
It was Moses’ own shame.
And maybe… that’s your battle too.

You feel God nudging you.
Calling you.
Pulling you toward something bigger than your comfort.
But there’s a voice inside you whispering—

“You’re not ready.”
“You’re not good enough.”
“You’ll mess this up.”

And just like Moses…
you start listing your weaknesses as if God didn’t already know them.
But here’s the tension we can’t ignore:
Why would a perfect God choose someone who feels broken?

Why would He call a man who struggles to speak…
to confront the most powerful ruler in the world?
That doesn’t make sense.
Unless…

God was never looking for ability.
He was looking for surrender.
Now watch this.

Moses stands in front of a burning bush—fire that doesn’t consume.
A holy moment.
A divine interruption.

And instead of confidence…
he offers excuses.

Exodus 4:10 —
“Pardon your servant, Lord. I have never been eloquent… I am slow of speech and tongue.”
Translation?
“I’m not built for this.”
“I’m not like them.”
“I’m not enough.”

And if we’re honest…
we’ve all prayed that prayer in different forms.

“I’m too broken.”
“My past is too messy.”
“My voice doesn’t matter.”
But here’s what we miss.
God doesn’t deny Moses’ weakness.
He reframes it.

Exodus 4:11 —
“Who gave human beings their mouths? Who makes them deaf or mute? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Is it not I, the Lord?”
Pause.
God is not intimidated by your limitation.
He’s not surprised by your insecurity.
He’s not scrambling because you feel inadequate.
He’s the Author of your design.
Even the parts you wish you could hide.

Some scholars interpret Moses’ “slow speech” as a stutter or speech impairment.
Others see it as lack of confidence or training.

But either way—
the point is clear:

Moses saw a flaw.
God saw a vessel.
And that’s where everything shifts.

Because your weakness…
is not an obstacle to God’s plan.
It’s the stage for His power.
But let’s go deeper.
The real issue wasn’t just Moses’ speech.
It was his heart posture.

Exodus 4:13 —
“Pardon your servant, Lord. Please send someone else.”
There it is.
Not just insecurity.
Resistance.

And if we’re real—
sometimes our “humility” is just fear wearing a holy mask.
We say, “I’m not worthy.”

But what we mean is,
“I don’t want to risk failure.”
We say, “I’m not ready.”

But what we mean is,
“I’m afraid of surrender.”
And that’s where conviction cuts deep.
Because God’s call will always confront your comfort.
It will always expose the places where you trust yourself more than Him.
But don’t miss this—
God didn’t cancel Moses.
He met him in it.

He gave him Aaron.
He gave him signs.
He gave him His presence.
Grace didn’t remove the weakness.
Grace walked with it.
And that points us straight to Jesus.

Because the greatest display of God’s power…
didn’t come through strength.
It came through what looked like weakness.

A beaten body.
A blood-stained cross.
A Savior who looked defeated.

1 Corinthians 1:27 —
“But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.”
Let that settle.
Jesus didn’t come for the polished.
He came for the broken.
Not the confident—
the desperate.
Not the ones who have it all together—
the ones who know they don’t.

Romans 5:8 —
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not when you fixed yourself.
Not when you improved.
While you were still messy.

Still doubting.
Still struggling.
Still saying, “I can’t.”
That’s when He said, “I will.”

And through His death and resurrection—
He didn’t just call you.
He made a way for you.
Sin separated you.
Jesus restored you.
Your failure disqualified you.
Jesus redeemed you.
Your shame silenced you.
Jesus gave you a new voice.
This is the Gospel.
Not self-improvement.
Not behavior modification.
But full, undeserved grace through Christ alone.

Ephesians 2:8–9 —
“For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith… not by works, so that no one can boast.”
So now the question isn’t:
“Are you good enough?”
The question is:
“Will you trust the One who is?”

Will you stop hiding behind your excuses…
and start walking in obedience?

Will you keep arguing with your calling…
or finally surrender to it?
Because God is still calling people who feel unqualified.
Still choosing the unlikely.
Still using voices that tremble.
The issue isn’t your weakness.
It’s your willingness.
So here it is—
Right now.
No more delay.
No more “maybe later.”
No more “send someone else.”
Say yes.

Say yes with your fear.
Say yes with your doubts.
Say yes with your imperfect voice.
Because God doesn’t need your perfection.
He wants your surrender.

And if you’ve never fully surrendered your life to Jesus—
this is your moment.

Turn from your sin.
Trust in Him.
Receive the grace you could never earn.
Let Him rewrite your story.

From shame… to redemption.
From fear… to calling.
